note: Tier armour is not loot: it is what a token turns into, so this dataset lists the 54 TOKENS and not the 200-odd pieces. Wowhead's guides rank the PIECES, which meant 492 BiS calls landed on items this site has no row for and every token showed a blank priority column. This maps each piece to the token that produces it, so the ring lands on the row that exists.
how: Generated, then checked. A token is uniquely identified by (tier, slot, class): tier comes from the set name, slot from the piece's own item data, class from the guide that names it. Every one of the 27 tier sets was verified against which classes actually name it in the guides - 549 rows, zero disagreements - so the set table is confirmed rather than remembered. Two candidates resolved to no token and are absent: Gyro-Balanced Khorium Destroyer and Libram of the Lightbringer, both non-armour items that merely contain a set name. Extended Sep 2026 with 58 more pieces, found by cross-referencing every id the guides name against loot_data.json once the Source column was captured. Each resolved the same way - tier and class from an already-mapped piece of the same set (the tooltip lists its siblings), slot from the piece's own item data - and the class groupings they produce reproduce the T4/T5-versus-T6 regrouping independently: Priest sits with Warrior below T6 and with Paladin at T6.
regenerate: The slots come from the item database and the pairs from data/loot_data.json; nothing here is guessed at runtime, which is why it is a reviewed file rather than a lookup fetch_bis.py performs.
